decisive_items: On MRI, the lesion was intradural and extramedullary, displaced the cauda equina ventrally, appeared faintly hyperintense on T1-weighted images, hypointense on T2-weighted images, and showed uniform contrast enhancement without a dural tail sign.
There was no clear continuity with the dura mater on imaging.
A 10-year-old boy presented with two months of progressively worsening low back pain and bilateral lower extremity pain, worse at night and on waking.
response.rationale: Pediatric age, lumbar intradural-extramedullary location, absent dural tail/dura continuity, and the imaging intensity profile favor clear cell meningioma, the more specific subtype explicitly considered in the vignette.

rejected.why: R1 names the broad meningioma category but lacks the specificity supported by the childhood presentation, lumbar location, lack of dural attachment, and imaging features that point toward clear cell meningioma.
